The camera is still broken, by the way. Some things never change.
Frame rate drops into the low twenties whenever more than three characters are on screen. I measured it.
The "HD" textures are upscaled, not native. Compare any signage at 1:1 and it is obvious.
Input latency is around 130ms on a standard HDMI chain, which is unacceptable for {genre}.
It does not hold sync on interlaced displays, which matters if you still run a CRT for the older systems.
For reference I am running component out into a calibrated set, so this is not a cabling issue.
Load times: 41 seconds from menu to gameplay on the stock drive, 28 after the drive swap.
The manual claims 60fps. It is 60 in menus. In gameplay it is a locked 30, which is fine, but say so.
Note that the {other_platform} version renders at a lower internal resolution than this one. Details in my profile.
Methodology as always: capture card, frame counter, three runs, worst case reported.
I tested on two consoles and three copies to rule out hardware, before anyone asks.
So where does that leave us? Somewhere frustratingly in the middle.
The good outweighs the bad, but only just, and only if you are patient.
I keep going back and forth on this one, which is itself a kind of verdict.
To be fair, the opening act shows real promise before it all goes sideways.
I will grant that the art team did their job; everyone else let them down.
If you liked the previous one, temper your expectations — this is a different animal.
It sits somewhere between the last two entries in quality, closer to the good one.
People compare it to the {platform} classics, and for once the comparison is not embarrassing.
In conclusion: not perfect, but essential. {title} will be remembered when this generation's shelf is cleared.

Native res is below the box's claim; I counted the jaggies so you don't have to.
Audio is compressed harder than it should be — cymbals turn to static in busy scenes.
The 30fps cap is fine; the 30fps cap that dips to 22 in cutscenes is not.
Install footprint is double the box quote once the day-one data lands.
Controller latency measured at the pad, not the panel: adds ~2 frames over last gen.
Draw distance pops in about forty feet out. Noticeable on the vehicle sections.
The 'widescreen' mode is a stretched 4:3 buffer. Look at the HUD circles and weep.
Anti-aliasing is doing nothing at this resolution; verify with a still and a magnifier.
Texture streaming stutters on the stock drive; the swap fixed 80% of it.
Color banding in the dark scenes screams 6-bit panel handling. Yours may vary.
The framerate graph is a saw blade, not a line. I have the capture if anyone doubts it.
Region-locked at the disc level, not the menu, before anyone asks the obvious.
Screen tearing with vsync OFF I expect; screen tearing with vsync ON is a bug.
It ignores the console's display settings entirely and forces its own gamma.
The netcode is peer-to-peer with no host migration. In 2011. Inexcusable.
Load-to-menu is 40 seconds, menu-to-game another 30. A minute of logo screens.
It doesn't buffer inputs during the animation, so combos drop for no reason.
The 'HD remaster' is the same assets at a higher output res. Upscale, not remaster.
Frame pacing is uneven even at a locked framerate — the judder is the tell.
It renders the UI at native but the world at 60% and never tells you.
Dolby on the box, stereo in practice. I checked the bitstream.
The patch that 'fixed' the framerate just lowered the resolution. I measured both.
Motion blur is masking the framerate, not enhancing the look. Turn it off and see.
It crashes on save if the card is over 80% full. Reproduced three times.
Test rig and full numbers are in my profile, as always.
Every figure here is a worst-case across three runs, not a cherry-picked best.
I disabled every enhancement setting to measure the game, not my TV.

Numbers taken with a frame counter overlay, not eyeballed. Eyeballing is how people get fooled.

Measured on a CRT and a calibrated flat panel to separate game from display.

Disc is flawless, artwork is sun-faded. A fair trade at this price.
Shrink-wrap intact but I opened it, because a game is for playing.
Comes with the pre-order pin nobody kept. That's the real find here.
'Complete' apparently no longer includes the manual. Since when?
Graded 'Like New' with a price sticker melted into the front. Do better.

The disc rattled in the case the whole way here. Zero padding.
Queued in the rain for this. The rain lost.
The whole line broke into the theme song at midnight. I'm not crying, you are.
Store ran out; the manager sold me the display copy off the wall. Legend.
Drove two towns over because my local didn't do a midnight. No regrets.
Met three people in that queue I still play with online. That's the series to me.
I'll be first in line for the next one regardless. You know this.
Twenty years in and they've earned the benefit of the doubt. This time.
This series raised me. I'm allowed to be a little biased about it.
Disc was cracked out of the shrink-wrap. Not a scratch — a crack. Took it straight back.
Wrong region entirely. Sealed, sold to me anyway, and then the 'refund' began.
The console died in nine days. Nine. Within every warranty they advertise.
Bought the wrong version by their own mislabeling and tried to return it same day.
So my cash becomes 'Bucks,' the Bucks have an expiry, and the shops have an expiry. Cute.
I asked for the manager. The manager also had EmporiumBucks and looked just as trapped.
It's my money with a leash on it and the leash is nailed to a sinking ship.
They call it store credit. I call it a coupon for a store that won't exist.
Three of the four stores I grew up with are shuttered now. You feel it walking in.
The staff are lovely and clearly know they're being wound down. It's grim.
Half the shelves are empty and the other half are 70% off. Read the room, it says.
Cost me less than the DLC costs the people who paid launch. Poetry.
At this price I'd forgive a lot, and happily I don't have to.
Cheaper than the strategy guide, and it IS the strategy guide, essentially.
Pound for pound the best thing in the bargain bin this quarter.
Even free would be steep once you count the hours it wasted.
Half price and still overpriced. That's a talent, really.
I've found better in the 'four for a fiver' box, and that box has standards.
The graphics are carrying a corpse and you're applauding the pallbearer.
Name one original idea in it. I'll wait. I've got all the time you spent defending it.
'It gets good after 20 hours' is the funniest sentence in this hobby.
Nostalgia is not a game mechanic, no matter how hard you review-bomb this.
You didn't like the game, you liked being fourteen. Understandable. Still one star.
Every fanbase gets the review it deserves. Say hi.
I'm not saying you have no taste. The rating is saying it for me.
Bold of a game this derivative to charge full price and bolder of you to pay it.
Take away the theme song and you've got a tech demo with a fanbase.
It's held up the way a museum piece holds up: behind glass, don't touch, don't question.
Groundbreaking in its day, sure. It is no longer its day.
The 'best game ever' according to people who stopped playing games that same year.
Docking half a star for the checkpoint before the final boss. You'll understand.
The map screen is a mess, but you memorise it eventually and stop caring.
One song on the soundtrack loops too short and now I can't unhear it.
The inventory limit is annoying but arguably keeps you honest.
A couple of difficulty spikes feel unplaytested, though nothing fatal.
The fast-travel unlocks about ten hours too late. Minor, but felt.
Some of the voice acting is rough; the lead carries it though.
The photo mode is bad, which shouldn't matter and somehow does.
I'll concede the boss design is smarter than the genre deserves.
The ending, and only the ending, justified the slog. Barely.
Against my nature, I have to admit the co-op is a good time.
Fine — the world is beautifully made. My quota of kindness is spent.
It does one thing right and it does it often enough that I finished it.
So do the highs outweigh the lows? On alternating days, yes.
It's a game I respect more than I enjoyed, if that distinction means anything.
I'd tell a friend to play it and warn them in the same breath.
It's the second-best game in its own series, which is either praise or a warning.
Think of the good one, subtract the confidence, add a year of delay. That's this.
If you bounced off the last one, this won't win you back.
Anyway. Stars above, take them or leave them.
That's my two cents, adjusted for inflation.
Do with this what you will; I've said my piece.
Off to play something else now. Probably.
